craft_notes: Sthāyin: vīra of fitted joinery — utsāha as qualifier meets qualified without loss. Ease-note opens mechanics: unity comes not hard — strainlessness as doctrine (consciousness-bodied need no forcing). Rejected: (a) is-not-difficult smoothing → killed: comes-not-hard keeps the coming. (b) cutting Māyā-differenced → killed: the hard case is the proof. Read aloud: SO, of-BE-ings, OF-con-scious-ness-BOD-ied BE-ings — … U-ni-ty COMES-not-HARD.

lines: So, of beings, of consciousness-bodied beings —
even Māyā-differenced, unity comes not hard.
l4.sanskrit_cite: evaṃ ca sati vastūnāṃ cinmātravapuṣāṃ satām māyānirmitabhedānāmapyekatvamadurghaṭam

reads_against.argmap: What of consciousness-bodied beings? → Even Māyā-differenced beings take unity without strain — for the consciousness-bodied.
c1_essence: Unity without strain for the consciousness-bodied; the worldly one's reflection-object fixed as difference-pithed non-difference-shining (vv10-11).
Mechanics: one thought un-touched, one word uniting many, helping relation admitted, twoness in manyness, two facings, three thinkings, genitive settling unself-lost (vv12-18).
